WITH b AS (SELECT unnest(generate_series(time_bucket(%s::INTERVAL, %s::TIMESTAMP), %s::TIMESTAMP, %s::INTERVAL)) AS bucket), c AS (SELECT time_bucket(%s::INTERVAL, ts) AS bucket, count(*) AS n FROM bgl WHERE true AND ts >= %s AND ts < %s AND component IN (%s) AND level IN (%s, %s) GROUP BY 1) SELECT b.bucket, coalesce(c.n, 0) FROM b LEFT JOIN c USING (bucket) WHERE b.bucket < %s ORDER BY 1

content.text:
**Top Components by FATAL+ERROR entries, both datasets** [E1]:

| Component | Entries | Share |
|---|---|---|
| KERNEL (BGL) | 626,450 | 64.7% |
| APP (BGL) | 228,536 | 23.6% |
| MMCS (BGL) | 88,532 | 9.2% |
| DISCOVERY (BGL) | 23,825 | 2.5% |
| LINKCARD (BGL) | 206 | <0.1% |
| oslo_service.periodic_task (OpenStack) | 184 | <0.1% |

That's 967,736 entries in total [E1]. OpenStack hardly shows up: it has no FATAL level, only 186 ERROR and 2 CRITICAL, and CRITICAL wasn't counted [E2]. BGL's SEVERE and FAILURE levels weren't counted either [E2].

**BGL KERNEL by week** [E3]: falling overall, but the pattern is one big burst that then dies down, not a steady decline.
- **Burst in June:** 152,521 entries in the week of 2005-06-06 and 377,594 in the week of 06-13. Those two weeks are about 85% of all KERNEL FATAL/ERROR entries.
- **Sharp drop:** 300 in the week of 06-20.
- **Smaller rise:** 9,339 in the week of 08-15, peaking at 17,597 in the week of 08-29, then 9,980 the week after.
- **Low weeks after that:** about 400–7,400 per week, with a small bump to 7,402 in the week of 11-14.
- **Last weeks:** 1,268, 797, then 477 in the week of 2006-01-02. That final week is incomplete because the data stops on 01-04.

These are counts of log entries, not incidents. One storm on a single node can make up a whole spike.
